summary: Check that every object claiming documented status resolves to a source locator and that interpretation stays separable.
objective: Each scene object carries a resolvable evidence category, and the exported artifact preserves that separation.
applies_when: A scene reconstructs a real site, artifact or period.
Some objects are evidence-based and others are invented to complete the picture.
The audience may reuse the image as documentation.
intent_signals: separate what is documented from what we invented
audit the provenance of this reconstruction
example_prompts: Audit which parts of this site reconstruction are actually documented.
negative_signals: inventing a fantasy setting with no real referent

principles: Evidence category is data attached to the object, not a colour convention; an object may be labelled documented only when it carries its own resolvable locator.
Interpretive reconstruction is legitimate and must stay visibly separable from documented remains at every zoom level and in every export.
One phase is one chronology; combining phases without saying so turns a reconstruction into an unattributed composite.
implementation: Build the inventory before modelling: object ID, evidence category (documented, inferred, invented), source locator, date or phase range, and the person who decided it.
Reconcile the inventory with the scene graph in both directions, so that every scene object resolves to a row and every documented row resolves to a locator a reader can open.
Sample at least one object per category, follow its locator to the passage or figure, and write down what the source actually shows and where it stops.
Export the categories with the artifact as a legend, data panel or written note; a category that exists only in the authoring session is not attribution.
observable_checks: No object keeps documented status without a resolvable locator; unresolved rows are downgraded to inferred or invented rather than left ambiguous.
Objects from different phases either share one declared phase or carry visible phase labels, and a mixed-phase view states that it is a composite.
The exported artifact reproduces the categories; losing them in export is a failure even when the authoring scene passed.

known_limits: An attribution procedure, not archaeological or historical peer review; a complete inventory does not make a reconstruction correct.
Authored verification guidance; no scene was run or rendered for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.
